sessions.title: Towards Decoding Dolphin Communication
sessions.titleIt: Towards Decoding Dolphin Communication
sessions.desc: For millennia humans have wondered what animals might be saying to each other, but (and not for lack of trying), we have never been able to decode their language. Modern machine learning systems have shown great promise and have already solved many problems previously thought to be impossible. This talk explores our efforts to use self-supervised machine learning to understand and interpret dolphin communication. First, we present a system that can "rediscover" the meaning of human language without a teacher, through watching unlabeled video. Second, we examine the challenge of applying these techniques to wild dolphin footage and share some preliminary techniques and observations.
sessions.hook: See how self-supervised machine learning rediscovers human language meaning and attempts to decode dolphin communication.
sessions.ideal: ML researchers and deep-tech enthusiasts curious about animal language.

sessions.title: Agentic AI for unstructured data: how to transform enterprise documents into operational knowledge
sessions.titleIt: Agentic AI per il dato destrutturato: come trasformare documenti aziendali in conoscenza operativa
sessions.desc:
In modern organizations, over 80% of information resides in unstructured content: documents, reports, procedures, proposals, knowledge bases, and historical archives. This represents a valuable asset that is often difficult to access, fragmented, and hard to leverage.
This talk explores how to design an Enterprise Agentic AI platform focused on corporate knowledge management to enable autonomous process orchestration, advanced document retrieval, and automated document generation.
The presented solution implements an adversarial Actor/Critic agentic model supported by a Reinforcement Learning system integrating RAG and GraphRAG engines, specialized agents for automated document generation, and advanced search capabilities across enterprise document repositories, with deployment options also in on-premise or isolated environments.
Special focus will be given to typical enterprise concerns often overlooked in AI projects, such as evolutionary maintenance, non-regression testing, performance benchmarking, observability, scalability, and operational continuity.
A real-world case demonstrates how agentic AI can evolve beyond a technological demo into an industrial-grade platform supporting business, operations, and decision-making.
sessions.hook: Design an enterprise agentic AI platform that turns unstructured documents into autonomous process orchestration and automated generation.
sessions.ideal: Enterprise architects and knowledge-management leads adopting agentic AI.

sessions.title: Arsenalia and the Municipality of Milan: practical AI in service of citizens
sessions.titleIt: Arsenalia e il Comune di Milano: AI concreta al servizio dei cittadini
sessions.desc: From the digital agent for registry and tax services to AI-based monitoring of building permits, from automatic anonymization in images related to penalties to NLP support for the 020202 contact center, up to the Extended Digital Twin for urban governance: the Municipality of Milan already has AI embedded in its processes. As the first Italian public administration with an AI Manifesto, Milan is the smartest city in Italy. Luca Curioni speaks with Antonio Zimmitti of Arsenalia about how an administration with 526 services and 3 million users per day is innovating in a concrete, ethical, and scalable way.
sessions.hook: See how Milan embeds AI in registry, tax, permits and contact-center services via its public AI Manifesto.

sessions.title: The real breakthrough in AI isn’t speed. It’s shared understandin
sessions.titleIt: La vera svolta dell’AI non è la velocità. È la comprensione condivisa.
sessions.desc:
Everyone is racing to make AI faster, cheaper, and bigger. But when the model speaks, does anyone actually understand?
In this session, Oddmund and Sven will unpack three gaps hiding in plain sight across the AI landscape and explain why the industry is obsessed with the first one while barely talking about the other two. They'll introduce the Comprehension Layer: the unsolved space between what AI produces and what humans actually need to understand, across languages, cultures, and high-stakes live environments. Drawing on Interprefy's experience powering real-time multilingual communication at scale , long before AI made it fashionable , this talk will challenge how the room thinks about what winning in AI actually looks like. Expect a frank conversation about infrastructure over hype, clarity over noise, and why the companies still standing in three years won't be the ones who shouted loudest. They'll be the ones who were most understood.
sessions.hook: Uncover three overlooked AI gaps and the Comprehension Layer bridging machine output and human understanding across languages.
sessions.ideal: Strategy and product leaders concerned with AI communication.

sessions.title: The death of software. Welcome to the era of processes.
sessions.titleIt: La morte del software. Benvenuti nell’era dei processi.
sessions.desc: Today’s software is like old phones: rigid, fragmented, and limited. The smartphone changed everything for people. Now the same thing is happening in companies: the operating system of processes is emerging. And after that, there’s no going back.
sessions.hook: Understand why rigid software is dying and how a process operating system reshapes companies irreversibly.
sessions.ideal: Founders and business leaders rethinking enterprise software.

sessions.title: MAaaP: Marketing Automation as a Playlist
sessions.titleIt: MAaaP: Marketing Automation as a Playlist
sessions.desc: Like a well-crafted playlist, the automation of the future starts, flows, and keeps things moving. But if no one takes care of it, it loops endlessly and loses its meaning. The marketer’s role? To stay firmly at the console, set the tempo, guide the tools, and read the audience in order to change the rhythm when needed.

sessions.title: From Earth Observation to Earth Intelligence: How the ESA Φ-lab helps developing solutions to Give the Planet a Voice
sessions.titleIt: Dall’osservazione della Terra all’intelligenza terrestre: come ESA Φ-lab contribuisce a sviluppare soluzioni per dare voce al pianeta.
sessions.desc:
Earth Observation data already supports decisions across many industries , often without anyone realizing it. Yet despite its enormous value, this data remains difficult to access, fragmented across platforms, and hard to translate into clear, decision-ready insights.
In this presentation, it will be shown how the ESA Φ-lab, and in particular the InCubed programme, supported two companies, GeoVille and Cortecs, to develop terrAIntel, an AI-powered Earth Intelligence platform designed to bridge this gap. The talk explores how AI can move users from programming languages and complex provider-specific workflows toward natural-language interaction, map-based evidence, statistics, and interpretation.
Rather than being another general-purpose LLM, terrAIntel is positioned as a domain-specialized AI layer that helps turn fragmented Earth Observation data into understandable and actionable Earth intelligence.
sessions.hook: See how ESA Phi-lab helped GeoVille and Cortecs build terrAIntel, turning Earth observation data into decision-ready intelligence.
sessions.ideal: Deep-tech and geospatial professionals working with Earth data.

sessions.title: AI tools applied to healthcare organizations

sessions.desc: AI on managers’ desks: what they really want to get from algorithms, between appropriateness, waiting lists, workflow efficiency, KPI optimization, and health demand analysis. Some suggestions to avoid selling just gadgets.

sessions.titleIt: Il Brand nell'Era dell'Intelligenza Artificiale

Together with EY Studio+, we will address key topics for brand growth in the age of artificial intelligence: authenticity as the only defense against algorithmic commoditization; human advantage as a source of competitive edge, where the more machines advance, the more the human element matters; monitoring and influencing positioning, and how to govern one’s narrative; and AI product design, focusing on how to build AI products that convey brand authenticity.

sessions.title: Governing AI: The Code of Conduct for Service Companies
sessions.titleIt: Governare l'AI: Il Codice di Condotta per le imprese di Servizi
sessions.desc:
Governing Artificial Intelligence means supporting its adoption with clear principles that guide its use in a responsible, transparent, and sustainable way.
In the context of professional services, this translates into defining a shared framework that places several key elements at its core: human oversight, skills development, transparency in decision-making processes, data protection, and risk management.
The goal is not to limit innovation, but to make it reliable and consistent with corporate values, fostering a conscious and long-lasting adoption of Artificial Intelligence.

sessions.title: The Soul of Efficiency in business process automation. Toward Wise Automation: Beyond the Algorithm, Toward Fairness.
sessions.titleIt: L'Anima dell'Efficienza nell’automazione dei processi aziendali. Verso un'Automazione Sapiente: Oltre l'Algoritmo, l'Equità.
sessions.desc: In an era dominated by the race for automation, the real risk is not technological but human: building perfect systems within an imperfect ecosystem. This talk proposes a paradigm shift, automation not as a replacement for human work, but as applied wisdom capable of elevating it. Through the real-world experience of the agents powering the SophIA and ThalIA platforms, the session explores three key pillars: • Automation as an ethical choice: designing fair and transparent processes, eliminating hidden biases in data and models. • Wisdom in automation: integrating a systemic vision that places the well-being of people and the organization at the center. • From productivity to human fulfillment: using AI to free up time and value, giving back to people what makes them unique, intuition, empathy, and judgment. The journey culminates in an evolved vision of the enterprise, where HR and Finance converge into a single connected intelligence, and where efficiency is no longer just a KPI, but the result of a harmonious balance between technology and humanity.
sessions.hook: Explore wise automation: designing fair, transparent, ethical processes that elevate human work, drawn from SophIA and ThalIA agents.
sessions.ideal: Leaders and strategists shaping ethical business automation.

sessions.titleIt: Insieme, costruiamo: dagli hack di AI all’infrastruttura di team
sessions.desc: We’re entering a new era of work, where AI isn’t a solo productivity hack, but something that lives inside a team’s shared space. Notion’s Yann Petretti will explore the productivity shift as organizations move from AI as an assistant to AI as a shared system: surfacing context, automating repetitive work, and helping teams make better decisions together. He’ll share a practical transformation path for leaders: how to adopt AI responsibly with guardrails, why proprietary context and connected tools matter, and what this shift means for European teams right now.
sessions.hook: Learn a leader's roadmap for moving AI from a solo assistant to a shared team system with responsible guardrails.
sessions.ideal: Business leaders and managers adopting AI across teams.

sessions.titleIt: Gli sviluppatori BI del futuro potrebbero non essere umani - Come tenere sotto controllo il tuo team AI nel BI Stack.

sessions.title: 30 days to start thinking again: how AI frees SME leaders from the work they shouldn’t be doing
sessions.titleIt: 30 giorni per tornare a pensare: come l'AI libera chi guida una PMI dal lavoro che non dovrebbe fare
sessions.desc: Every entrepreneur knows what they should be doing with their time: making strategic decisions, spending time with customers, and growing their people. Yet the day gets taken up by something else: checking numbers, reminding the team about deadlines, and searching for information scattered across spreadsheets, Excel files, emails, and messages. sessions.title: Artificial intelligence at work: real cases of operational transformation in complex organizations.
sessions.titleIt: L'intelligenza artificiale al lavoro: casi reali di trasformazione operativa nelle organizzazioni complesse
sessions.desc:
What would happen if every employee always had access to an expert, trained on your documentation, your processes, and your regulations, ready to respond in real time, without ever forgetting anything?
In this session, Marco Cavallini (CEO of YouCo) presents YouWorker.ai: YouCo’s AI system that learns an organization’s knowledge and operates autonomously within a closed, secure, and GDPR-compliant environment, integrating into daily operations without disrupting existing processes.
To ground the proposal, two real-world case studies:
Stefano Crotti (IT & AI Program Manager, COREPLA) explains how Italy’s National Consortium for the Collection and Recycling of Plastic Packaging transformed a complex and fragmented document heritage into an immediate operational tool, reducing information retrieval times and increasing operational speed.
Ester Anzalone (Director of Digital Transformation, Metropolitan City of Milan) illustrates how an organization serving 133 municipalities and 3.2 million citizens deployed an AI agent to support citizens 24/7, reduce response times, and free operators from repetitive requests, while ensuring full compliance with AgID guidelines and ACN regulations.
A session focused on concrete AI already in action: not a promise, but a replicable model.

However, the main challenge remains turning this infrastructure into real-world usage. In this context, Villanova acts as an enabling layer: through generative AI, multimodal models, and a low-code/no-code framework, it allows companies and public administrations to develop concrete applications on the European cloud-edge. In this session, Matteo Brusco, Distribution Sales Manager Southern Europe at N-able, will present N-able’s vision for AI applied to IT management, cybersecurity, and operational automation, with a focus on N-zo, the AI assistant integrated into the N-able ecosystem.
N-zo is designed to support technicians, MSPs, IT teams, and security teams in the daily management of increasingly distributed infrastructures: from device status summarization to troubleshooting, from vulnerability analysis to intelligent documentation search, and toward future scenarios of agentic automation. The goal is simple yet strategic: reduce time spent on repetitive tasks, improve decision quality, and strengthen business operational resilience.
Through concrete use cases, customer feedback, and an evolving roadmap focused on AI assistants, expert agents, predictive automation, and cross-platform workflows, the session will show how N-able is transforming AI into a true ally for efficiency, security, and business continuity. The presentation highlights measurable benefits, including an average time saving of around 70% and operational speed improvements of 2, 5x in common documentation and troubleshooting tasks.

sessions.desc:
The study analyzes a global e-commerce system using AutoCM and Meta-AutoCM models to go beyond traditional sales statistics.
AutoCM identifies direct associations between variables (markets, products, platforms), while Meta-AutoCM reveals functional similarities and systemic impact.
Results show that geography is the main driver, with markets influencing the system far more than product categories.
It highlights “sentinel” markets that detect early changes and “bridge” countries that signal their spread toward Europe and the US.
The combined approach provides a strategic map for geographic segmentation, early-warning monitoring, and optimization of pricing and sales strategies.
sessions.hook: Apply AutoCM and Meta-AutoCM neural models to e-commerce, revealing geography as main driver and sentinel and bridge markets.

sessions.title: Now That Everyone Can Build

sessions.desc:
A keynote on why the next era of AI will not be defined only by better tools, but by more people choosing to act like founders.
For decades, software creation was constrained by access: access to technical skills, teams, capital, and institutional permission. Lovable is changing that. More people can now move from idea to working product faster than ever before. As building becomes easier, founder-like behaviours become more important: ownership, speed, judgement, resilience, and the ability to learn in public.
Aino will argue that the underlying shift is behavioural. The people who stand out in the AI era are those who see a gap, take ownership, learn quickly, build something real, and find the community or market that needs it. Being a founder is becoming a way of operating that can apply far beyond the traditional startup path. Drawing on her experience building Europe’s startup community at Slush, and now leading special projects, community and growth initiatives at Lovable, Aino will explore what happens when software creation opens up to the 99% in the broadest behavioural sense. More people can now participate in building products, companies, communities and new economic value. But building is only the beginning. The founders who win are the ones who turn access into action, action into momentum, and momentum into impact.
The central question is shifting from whether people can build, to what they choose to take responsibility for next.
sessions.hook: Hear why the AI era rewards founder behaviours, ownership and speed as building products becomes accessible to everyone.
sessions.ideal: Founders, builders, aspiring entrepreneurs

The panel presents the vision of the Department of Public Administration of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers on the use of intelligent agents in managing public human capital, starting from a crucial area: the onboarding of new employees and staff in mobility. Entering public administration is the moment when a person comes into contact with processes, skills, responsibilities, professional communities, and the sense of public service. From this perspective, agents can support people in navigating processes, accessing internal knowledge, understanding procedures, assessing entry-level skills, activating personalized training pathways, and connecting with tutors, experts, and similar profiles. The goal is to make onboarding more scalable, consistent, and personalized, without replacing the human role and the responsibility of public institutions. The panel also explores the vision of an agentic ecosystem for public administration: modular, secure, and interoperable solutions capable of supporting not only onboarding, but also training, internal mobility, performance, attractiveness, and knowledge transfer. A new infrastructure to strengthen administrative capacity and make institutional knowledge more accessible. At the core remains an institutional choice: using AI to augment people, not to reduce them to process endpoints; to strengthen skills, responsibility, and organizational quality.

sessions.title: Unsupervised Learning for Discovering Structure in Complex Systems
sessions.titleIt: Unsupervised Learning for Discovering Structure in Complex Systems
sessions.desc: How does the human mind make sense of raw information without being taught how to see or hear? In this talk we will explore how to build algorithms that can uncover interpretable structure from large collections of unsupervised data like images and video. First, I will describe how to classify every pixel of a collection of images without any human annotations (Unsupervised semantic segmentation) by distilling self-supervised vision models. Second, we’ll see how this basic idea leads us to a new unifying theory of representation learning, and I will show how 20 different common machine learning methods such as dimensionality reduction, clustering, contrastive learning, and spectral methods emerge from a single unified equation. Finally, we’ll use this unified theory to create algorithms that can decode natural language just by watching unlabeled videos of people talking, without any knowledge of text. This work is the first step in our broader effort to translate animals using large scale, unsupervised, and interpretable learners, and the talk will conclude with some of our most recent efforts to analyze the complex vocalizations of Atlantic spotted dolphins.
sessions.hook: Learn to build algorithms that classify every image pixel without human annotations by distilling self-supervised vision models.

sessions.desc: What if machine learning had its own periodic table, not of atoms but of algorithms? In this talk, I’ll share how our team of researchers from MIT, Microsoft, and Google discovered a single equation that unifies over 20 foundational AI methods, from clustering to contrastive learning, into one simple, elegant framework. Just as the periodic table revealed hidden patterns in chemistry, our "Periodic Table of Machine Learning" uncovers deep connections between seemingly unrelated algorithms and even reveals entirely new ones waiting to be explored. Beyond theory, this perspective enabled us to build unsupervised AI systems that classify images with no human labels, outperforming previous state-of-the-art methods. It’s a story of simplicity beneath complexity, and how uncovering structure can spark breakthroughs.

sessions.title: True, plausible-indeed, likely. AI as an opaque, statistically reliable oracle
sessions.titleIt: Vero, verosimile anzi probabile. L’AI come oracolo opaco statisticamente sicuro
sessions.desc: Artificial intelligence does not tell the truth. Not even what is merely plausible, for that matter. It tells what is probable, more precisely, what is statistically least wrong among a billion possible attempts. And yet we treat it like an oracle: instant answers, confident tone, no hesitation. But beneath the glossy surface of generative and predictive algorithms lies a troubling opacity: no one, not even those who designed them, can truly explain why the AI responded the way it did. Its certainty is only statistical: it works on average, not in the individual case. This talk dismantles the illusion of the transparent oracle and exposes the radical difference between being true and simply not having been disproven by the distribution curve. Between truth and plausibility, a void opens up, one that AI fills with probabilities trained on past data, often biased, always finite. The result is a paradox: the more statistically reliable AI becomes, the greater the risk that we mistake the probable for the authentic. A provocation to rethink our relationship with machines that do not know what truth is, yet are remarkably good at pretending they do.
sessions.hook: Examine why generative AI outputs the statistically least-wrong answer, not truth, and why even its designers cannot explain it.
sessions.ideal: Ethicists, policymakers and critical-thinking professionals.

sessions.title: Sovereignty à la carte: how much freedom do you want over your data?
sessions.titleIt: Sovranità à la carte: quanta libertà vuoi sui tuoi dati?
sessions.desc:
Imagine a scale. At the bottom, your data travels on third-party infrastructure, encrypted with keys that , in theory , only you control. One step above, you truly hold those keys yourself. Higher up, the software processing your data is open, auditable, and modifiable. At the top, the entire platform runs within your perimeter, on hardware you can physically touch.
There is no single model of sovereignty. There are levels. And each level comes with a cost, an advantage, and a promise.
In this workshop, we take a journey through this scale , practical, without dogma. We start with hyperscalers , Google Cloud, Microsoft , and examine what it really means to rely on them while holding the encryption keys: what is protected, what is not, and when it is enough. Then we move up: Customer-Managed Keys, BYOK (Bring Your Own Key), all the way to models where the key never leaves your system.
We then reach hybrid AI platforms, built for example on enterprise Kubernetes stacks, where data never leaves your datacenter but cloud power remains accessible. And finally, we reach the top: fully open-source models deployed in completely controlled environments, where every line of code is inspectable and no vendor can change the rules mid-game.
The question is not “which level is best.” The question is: which level is right for you, today, given your regulatory constraints, your industry, and your risk appetite?
A healthcare organization handling patient data does not have the same needs as a fintech startup in a testing phase. A European public administration under the post-AI Act framework does not think like an e-commerce optimizing product recommendations. Sovereignty is not one-size-fits-all. And that is exactly why we have chosen to build a proposal that spans the entire scale: because we believe our job is not to sell a technology, but to help you understand how much freedom you need , and then give it to you. With hyperscalers when enough, with open source when full control is required. We are not here to tell you that the cloud is the enemy. We are here to tell you that the choice must be yours. Informed. Conscious. Reversible. Because true data sovereignty does not start from the server where the model runs. It starts the moment you realize you have the ability to choose.
sessions.hook: Navigate the levels of data sovereignty, from third-party keys to fully owned hardware, weighing each level's cost and advantage.
sessions.ideal: IT, security, cloud and data governance leaders.

sessions.title: Investigative AI: Legal and Illegal Economies. Investigative AI: Intelligence Topology of Terroristic Attacks
sessions.titleIt: Investigative AI: Legal and Illegal Economies. Investigative AI: Intelligence Topology of Terroristic Attacks
sessions.desc:
This presentation introduces an Investigative AI framework built on artificial neural networks
developed at the Semeion Research Center (Rome), specifically AutoCM (Auto-Contractive Map) and Meta-AutoCM. The analysis is applied to a dataset of 120 monthly observations (2016, 2025) across 32 heterogeneous variables spanning corporate profits, energy markets, military expenditure, illegal markets, criminal trafficking, geopolitics, financial opacity, and cognitive-political dynamics (social media, polarization, disinformation). The work distinguishes two prediction paradigms , probabilistic (classical pattern recognition) and harmonic (weak present-day signals that foreshadow major future events) , and presents a three-stage analytical pipeline: PCA for initial orientation, AutoCM for first-order topology ("who is linked to whom";), and Meta-AutoCM for second-order functional topology ("who acts like whom"). Key findings show that the variables with the highest Activation Force in the system are not the large legal economic actors but rather illegal or extreme nodes , fentanyl (Act = 1.000), cocaine, terrorism, diamonds , which operate as high-perturbation triggers with few connections but strategic positioning. Legal and institutional nodes (Meta Platforms, cryptocurrency, Lockheed, social media) dominate connectivity and serve as signal amplifiers and redistributors. AutoCM reveals a concrete structural corridor: drugs → diamonds → energy → refugees → military apparatus. Meta-AutoCM uncovers unexpected
functional equivalences (Meta ≈ Crypto ≈ Lockheed) and demonstrates that JPMorgan is peripheral, with zero activation. A bootstrap validation across five 75%-subsamples confirms the granite stability of the trigger core and the fluidity of the redistribution apparatus. The central thesis is that economic volume does not equate to structural power: systemic control arises from the
coupling of a few illegal ignition points with legal amplification corridors.
sessions.hook: Apply Semeion's AutoCM and Meta-AutoCM neural networks to map legal-illegal economies and terrorism across 32 variables over a decade.
sessions.ideal: Researchers, analysts, policy and intelligence professionals

sessions.title: UNaIVERSE: Autonomous Digital Societies for Humans and Decentralized AI
sessions.titleIt: UNaIVERSE: Autonomous Digital Societies for Humans and Decentralized AI
sessions.desc:
UNaIVERSE is an innovative startup that introduces a transformative approach to the technological stack, moving "above" standard Agentic AI frameworks to create autonomous communities of humans and AIs. By leveraging peer-to-peer (P2P) networks, UNaIVERSE enables private, on-premise implementations of complex industrial processes, bypassing the risks of centralized cloud infrastructures, promoting control and integration with heterogeneous systems, beyond LLM-centric frameworks. While modern web and social AI systems have expanded human capability, they have also compromised privacy, centralized power, and created unsustainable energy demands. UNaIVERSE advocates for a fundamental paradigm shift grounded in privacy preservation, energy efficiency, and distributed design, as championed by Collectionless AI. Key highlights of this speech: (1) The Shift to the Edge: Relocating intelligence from centralized servers to edge devices. This utilizes local computational power while maintaining sophisticated, integrative information sharing and long-term learning. (2) The "Worlds" Concept: A re-organization of the Web into autonomous ecosystems. These "Worlds" function as digital societies where agents learn, reason, and plan based on collective constraints and shared intents. (3) Decentralized Protocols: Utilizing P2P communication to ensure that individual and collective goals are met without intermediary surveillance.
We will demonstrate how UNaIVERSE instantiates this vision, providing a platform where decentralized AI and human-AI coexistence are governed by privacy-first principles.
sessions.hook: Discover UNaIVERSE's peer-to-peer approach building autonomous human-AI communities with private on-premise deployments beyond centralized cloud and LLM-centric frameworks.
sessions.ideal: Researchers and architects building decentralized AI systems.

sessions.title: Approved, developed, wrong. The invisible cost that AI is multiplying
sessions.titleIt: Approvato, sviluppato, sbagliato. Il costo invisibile che l'AI sta moltiplicando
sessions.desc: Every digital project has a moment when its fate is decided. It is usually not when the software goes into production. It happens much earlier , in a meeting where everyone nods, but no one has truly seen. Unvalidated flows, ignored exceptions, expectations that seem shared but are not: these are not technical problems. They are decisions made in the dark. And the bill comes later, in the form of rework, delays, and budgets that never add up. Today, AI introduces a variable that changes everything: it can compress development times, automate processes, and multiply execution speed. But if the project starts off wrong, AI does not fix it , it accelerates it. It automates ambiguity. It scales error. It makes a merely plausible project more expensive, and faster. Anyone developing software sees it every day: the problem almost never starts in the code. It starts in the moment when someone said “we understand each other” and it wasn’t true. This talk explores that moment: where digital initiative risk truly originates, why managers approve with less information than they believe, and what mindset shift is needed to see before deciding , not to build more, but to get things wrong much less.
sessions.hook: Understand how unvalidated flows and decisions made in the dark multiply hidden AI project costs through rework and delays.
sessions.ideal: CDOs and project leaders managing digital delivery.

While the concept of the “AI Factory” is gaining traction, much of its current implementation follows an extractive model, energy-intensive, water-consuming, and often misaligned with local communities.
This talk introduces Water-to-Token, a new paradigm for AI infrastructure developed by Terakraft. By repurposing a decommissioned hydropower plant, we demonstrate how AI compute can be powered entirely by renewable energy while leveraging natural water flows for efficient cooling. The result is a closed-loop system that minimizes environmental impact while maximizing energy efficiency.
Beyond technology, we explore a fundamentally different approach to infrastructure development: one that integrates local economies, gains community support, and reinforces European digital sovereignty. By involving regional partners and ensuring European ownership, the model aligns environmental sustainability with social and governance responsibility.
sessions.hook: Discover Water-to-Token: repurposing a decommissioned hydropower plant into a sustainable European AI compute factory aligned with local communities.

sessions.title: Your Brain on ChatGPT
sessions.titleIt: Your Brain on ChatGPT
sessions.desc:
Join Dr. Nataliya Kosmyna of the MIT Media Lab for a discussion on the use of AI and its effects on the human brain.
For millions of years, human intelligence set the standard. But now, the lightning pace of tech has left us gasping, struggling to keep up with our own cognitive demands. AI has pushed civilization into overdrive, yet what we are ultimately doing is burning terawatts of power on data centers and excluding humans from this growth. We have built systems that are prefixed ‘smart’, but not smart enough to break free from their own inefficiency. Technology should amplify our creativity, not snuff it out. It should fuel social interactions, not isolate us. Instead, we are trapped in a dystopian remix of 1984, 2026’s version, where digital censorship and surveillance threaten to choke innovation in nations that refuse to play along. This talk will explore critical questions: What should define ownership in the age of AI and at what cost?
Dr. Kosmyna is a research scientist at MIT Media Lab’s Fluid Interfaces group and a Visiting Research Faculty at Google. She has over 16 years of experience in developing and designing end-to-end brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). Coming from a background in artificial intelligence, neuroscience, and human computer interaction, she is passionate about the idea of creating a partnership between AI and human intelligence, a fusion of the machine with the human brain.
sessions.hook: Hear MIT Media Lab's Dr. Nataliya Kosmyna on how using ChatGPT and AI affects the human brain and cognition.
sessions.ideal: Anyone curious about AI's cognitive impact

sessions.desc: The past 30 years have marked an unprecedented historical period in the democratization of information. The emergence and evolution of the web, first, and the arrival of social media later, have enabled anyone with internet access to share their thoughts in their most absolute form of freedom, without the mediation of traditional media. However, what once seemed like the beginning of a golden age now confronts us with a paradox: we find ourselves trapped within frameworks built by a few major global information holders, using the very data that all of us have made freely available online over time. Based on these data, these same actors have created the large models for artificial intelligence that we use every day, both in our personal and professional lives, giving us a second illusion of innovation and freedom, despite clear side effects. The use of external services indeed enables immediate scalability, but it also introduces significant challenges when it comes to sensitive or proprietary data. The continuous transfer of information to third-party environments, technological dependency on the provider, the difficulty of predicting operational costs, energy inefficiency, and compliance implications make these models at least debatable. For Europe, this evolution also takes on a broader strategic dimension. Digital sovereignty is not only about data localization, but about the ability to control critical technologies. Fully relying on non-European infrastructures for information processing means exposing oneself to industrial and geopolitical vulnerabilities. So, let us ask ourselves: are we truly free, sovereign? And, above all, digitally autonomous? How can we reverse this trend over the next 30 years?
sessions.hook: Examine how a few global platforms trap our digital freedom, and what reclaiming digital autonomy demands.
sessions.ideal: Founders, leaders, policy-minded tech professionals

sessions.title: Lost in Translation? How a translation agency reinvented its future in the age of AI.
sessions.titleIt: Lost In Translation? Come un’agenzia di traduzioni ha reinventato il suo futuro nell’era dell’IA.
sessions.desc: The talk tells the story of how Intrawelt, a translation agency from the Marche region with 35 years of experience in translation, localization, and interpreting services, responded to the challenge of AI instead of being overwhelmed by it, in collaboration with the SPOCRI Lab of the University of Macerata led by Professor Emanuele Frontoni. Starting from the catastrophic predictions surrounding the industry, the presentation shows how the global translation market has actually continued to grow (+5.6% annually, from USD 56 billion to a projected USD 124 billion by 2037), while still acknowledging the real impact on professionals in the sector. Intrawelt’s response was the development of scenia®, a SaaS platform created in collaboration with the University of Macerata and the company Aidapt. The platform integrates translation memories, specialized AI, and human professionals (human-in-the-loop) into a model where costs progressively decrease as validated translation knowledge accumulates. The core thesis is that translation and AI have become commodities, but the real product has always been , and still is , the expert management of complex linguistic projects.
sessions.hook: Hear how a 35-year translation agency reinvented itself with AI instead of being disrupted by it.
